title: Capacitor
content: A capacitor is an electrical device that stores electrical energy in the form of an electrical field.
e: Capacitor: A capacitor is an electrical device that stores electrical energy in the form of an electrical field. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

title: Capacitance (C)
content: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the charge to the potential difference of the capacitor.
e: Capacitance (C): The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the charge to the potential difference of the capacitor. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current.

title: One Farad
content: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1 V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is 1 C V⁻¹ (or) 1 F. Therefore, 1 Farad is equivalent to 1 C V⁻¹.
e: One Farad: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1 V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is 1 C V^-1 (or) 1 F. Therefore, 1 Farad is equivalent to 1 C V^-1. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

title: Electric capacity of the conductor
content: The amount of charge given to a conductor to change its potential by one unit is called the electric capacity of the conductor.
e: Electric capacity of the conductor: The amount of charge given to a conductor to change its potential by one unit is called the electric capacity of the conductor. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.

title: Parallel-plate capacitor
content: A parallel-plate capacitor is the simplest capacitor. It consists of two parallel metal plates separated by air or other insulating material.
e: Parallel-plate capacitor: A parallel-plate capacitor is the simplest capacitor. It consists of two parallel metal plates separated by air or other insulating material. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows.

title: Charging a Capacitor
content: Charging a capacitor means connecting the capacitor to a battery.
e: Charging a capacitor means connecting the capacitor to a battery. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

title: Dielectric constant (κ)
content: The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of vacuum. Alternatively, it is the ratio of the capacitance of a capacitor with an insulating material between its two conductors to the capacitance of that capacitor with a vacuum between its two conductors.
e: Dielectric constant (κ): The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of vacuum. Alternatively, it is the ratio of the capacitance of a capacitor with an insulating material between its two conductors to the capacitance of that capacitor with a vacuum between its two conductors. The plates must conduct so charge can spread; the gap must insulate or the field collapses.

title: Time constant (τ)
content: The product of the resistance R and the capacitance C is called the time constant τ of a capacitor charging or discharging process. It is measured in second.
e: Time constant (τ): The product of the resistance R and the capacitance C is called the time constant τ of a capacitor charging or discharging process. It is measured in second. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.
